forecasts.reason: Running the 28 px phase at 24 px cuts pixel-weighted compute by about 8% (772→710), so time falls about 7%. Moving those mid-phase steps down to 24 px should cost about 0.2 pp against a true mean of about 0.757. That lands around the bar, and ±0.3 pp of reshuffle hides whether the 32 px phase alone sets accuracy.

E017 matched E016's math but scored 0.7537, which puts the true mean near 0.756–0.757. A 10-seed mean of 0.757 or more would sit about 0.4 pp or further below 0.7607, outside H4.1.3's 0.05–0.3 pp offset window, and a rebuild with a fresh cache probably shifts the mean by more than 0.25 pp.

Cutting from 238 to 213 steps removes about 10.5% of time after the fixed cost. At about 0.2 pp per 0.5 epoch, a true mean near 0.757 drops to about 0.753, a coin flip at the bar. One 3-seed point cannot resolve the slope within noise.

Narrowing group 2 to 320 cuts its 384→384 convs by 31% and group 3's first conv by 17%, about 13–15% of FLOPs and roughly 9% of time. Group 2 is the main 8×8 feature stage for 100 classes, so I expect a loss of more than 0.25 pp.

Filters are renormalized, so this is effectively a global cut. Weight decay on the head and BN biases was over-regularizing, but a second halving gives diminishing returns, maybe +0.1 pp of real gain. The 3-seed comparison against the 0.7607 baseline is swamped by about ±0.3 pp of reshuffle.

Group 1's conv3 is only about 36% of group 1's MACs (conv1 has just 24 input channels), or about 6.5% of FLOPs plus some BN/GELU memory traffic. That gives roughly 6% less time, below the 8% bar, and losing depth early in the network for 100 classes probably costs 0.3–0.5 pp.

Running the first 15% of steps at 20 px instead of 24 px cuts only about 3.4% of pixel-weighted compute, so time falls about 3%, below the 4% bar. Group 3's 2×2 maps at 20 px add a further accuracy cost.

cruxes: What is the 10-seed held-out mean of the E016/E017 recipe? If it is about 0.757, the 0.3–0.4 pp needed for any trim exists. If it is about 0.754, every time cut must be paired with an accuracy gain.

How much does an identical-math rebuild move the mean? E016→E017 moved it 0.7 pp. If kernel reselection really causes swings that large, single 3-seed keep decisions are mostly noise and the 40-seed judge needs about 0.3 pp of headroom.
Does accuracy live in the 32 px tail? If I029 holds accuracy within 0.15 pp, the cheapest remaining time lever is moving more early steps to 24 px rather than cutting width or depth.

W1 (mechanism), after E017. The tip is E017: E016's math with graph breaks removed. It scores 6.548 s and 0.7537, only 0.07 pp above the 0.753 bar.

The code shows 238 steps, which is 9.5 true epochs. Muon renormalizes the filters and never applies weight decay, so weight decay only acts on the SGD groups (head and BN biases). Newton-Schulz already runs 3 iterations. Graph-break removal saved only 0.5% of time.

The E016→E017 change of −0.7 pp on identical math means reshuffle noise is about ±0.35 pp. I put the true mean at about 0.756–0.757.

Time is about 0.35 s fixed plus a part proportional to pixel-weighted conv FLOPs. Ranked by expected cost:
- Swapping 28 px steps for 24 px: about −7% time for about −0.2 pp. Cheapest per pp.
- Cutting epochs: about −0.4 pp per 10% time.
- Narrowing group 2 or removing depth: about −0.5 pp or more per 10% time.
- A 20 px stage: a cliff.

Margin is nearly gone, so time cuts need accuracy boosts paired with them. Candidate boosts are a further weight-decay cut and BN-statistics recalibration.
